title: The remaining CLI stubs print success to stdout and exit 0
description:
The generalisation of persona-5s4b.103, for the commands that pass were not in that bead's scope. Each prints a not-implemented notice with println! (stdout) and returns Ok, so the exit status is 0:

- fetch_x509, main.rs:386. Aggravated by the stream choice: this command's whole purpose is to emit a credential to stdout, so 'persona fetch-x509 > client.pem' writes a file containing 'X.509-SVID issuance not yet implemented (persona-4qm)' and reports success. Whatever consumes client.pem fails later, in a component with no idea the CLI was a stub. The bead number in the message is good practice and should survive the fix.
- trust_bundle 'add', main.rs:431-433. The URL argument is read nowhere in the function; args is only consulted for the subcommand. 'persona trust-bundle add https://peer.example && mark_federation_ready' succeeds, and so does the same command with no URL at all -- there is no arity check. Silently discarding an argument removes the signal an operator uses to tell a stub from a real command.
- the trust_bundle _ arm, main.rs:437-439, prints usage to stdout and returns Ok. So 'persona trust-bundle lst' succeeds. Both comparable dispatchers in the same file exit 1 on an unrecognised word (enroll's, and the top-level one), making this the only unknown-subcommand path a shell gate treats as done.

trust-bundle remove is filed separately because it is fail-open rather than fail-closed.
acceptance_criteria: Each stub exits non-zero; not-implemented notices go to stderr, not stdout; unknown trust-bundle subcommands exit non-zero.
close_reason: Fixed in 440c6eb: fetch-x509, trust-bundle add and trust-bundle remove write to stderr and exit 1; the trust-bundle unknown-subcommand arm exits 1 like enroll's and main's. Verified by running: 'persona fetch-x509 > FILE' now leaves FILE 0 bytes with exit 1. Also added --help arms to both dispatchers, which unwrap_or("--help") had made answer 'unknown subcommand: --help'.
